chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Al-wala' (the right of manumission/kinship by contract) is flesh like the flesh of lineage; it is not sold and it is not given as a gift.'

key_terms.تُوهَبُ: It is given as a gift

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of al-wala' and can it be sold or gifted?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on manumission, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (via the Prophet) defines 'al-wala'' as an intrinsic bond ('lun'ah') comparable to kinship, thereby prohibiting its alienation through sale or gift. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the right of manumission is a permanent, non-transferable attribute of the master, preserving the social and economic integrity of the freed slave's relationship with their original owner.
